Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestJulianChronology_test_LocalDate_from_JulianDate.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestJulianChronology/TestJulianChronology_test_LocalDate_from_JulianDate.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The original test contains seven `data_*` provider methods but only `data_samples` is actually wired to a test (`@MethodSource("data_samples")`). The other six are dead code, and most imports support only that dead code. I'll keep the single executed test's behavior identical while removing the noise and making the data readable.Compiles cleanly (`COMPILE_OK`). I improved understandability by removing the six unused `data_*` provider methods and their supporting imports (all dead code, never referenced by any test), then reformatting the executed `data_samples` into grouped, commented rows that explain the Julian↔ISO alignment offset and leap-year cases. The one actual test still calls `LocalDate.from(julian)` and asserts equality against the same expected dates, so runtime behavior is unchanged.
